candidates.name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: A Snowflake + DBT data-warehouse pipeline built on "over 35 million records from 2015-2020" sourced from Inside Airbnb (CC0), Kaggle World Cities Population/Location, and Numbeo Cost of Living. Star-schema fact/dimension tables for studying Airbnb's effect on housing across multiple world cities. 68 commits. It is a pipeline/warehouse project, not obviously a committed flat-file archive — needs a closer look (via gh, later) to see whether raw 2015-2020 Inside Airbnb snapshots are stored anywhere retrievable (release assets, seed CSVs) versus only re-derivable by re-running against Inside Airbnb's live (now-pruned) archive.
candidates.why_useful: If the underlying 2015-2020 raw Inside Airbnb dumps are actually retrievable from this repo/its history, it could plug gap #1 (historical Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023, now off the CDN) for multiple cities beyond our 13-city panel.
candidates.size_hint: 35M+ records claimed across three source datasets
candidates.license: Source data CC0; repo license not confirmed
candidates.last_activity: unconfirmed (WebFetch summary did not surface a date)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Overlaps our 13-city Inside Airbnb panel (Dec 2022-Aug 2026) only if it turns out to hold the pre-2023 years we are missing

candidates.name: pit-fundamentals
candidates.what_it_holds: data/pit_fundamentals_history.csv (6,969 rows), plus query_asof.py (point-in-time query tool) and check_your_data.py (lookahead-bias checker). Covers 40 large-cap US companies, 16 financial concepts, each row stamped with period_end, first_filed (public-disclosure date), lag_days, original_value, latest_value, restated flag. ~12 years of revenue history per company. Source: SEC EDGAR (public domain), CC0-licensed. Rebuilt 7 Sep 2026, 36 commits.
candidates.why_useful: Directly implements gap #4's method (point-in-time fundamentals with no lookahead bias) as a reusable, license-clean pattern; even if ABNB/OTAs are not among the 40 tickers (unconfirmed), the query_asof.py + methodology is a ready-made PIT harness we could apply to ABNB's own EDGAR filings, which is exactly the discipline our CLAUDE.md rule #2 already requires.

candidates.name: restaurant-industry-amidst-covid19
candidates.what_it_holds: YoY_Seated_Diner_Data.csv and YoY_Reopened_Seated_Diner_Data.csv — OpenTable's year-over-year seated-diners series, downloaded from the OpenTable website 21 Jul 2020, plus a NYT us-states.csv COVID case-count file pulled 26 Jul 2020. US state-level coverage, single point-in-time pull (mid-2020 only).
candidates.why_useful: Matches gap #6 (OpenTable seated-diners as a public consumer-spend/dining-out proxy); useful mainly as a worked example of scraping/parsing OpenTable's public State-of-the-Industry page and as a one-time historical anchor point, not an ongoing feed.

candidates.name: machine-learning-for-trading
candidates.what_it_holds: Companion code repo for the "Machine Learning for Algorithmic Trading" book. Chapter 4 ("Fundamental and Alternative Data") documents point-in-time SEC EDGAR pipelines, entity resolution across identifier systems, macro/commodity fundamentals, and alternative-data evaluation frameworks (including newer additions like on-chain/prediction-market data). Earlier editions of this repo are widely known to include an OpenTable scraping chapter and other alt-data acquisition notebooks (Twitter/SEC filings/Seeking Alpha) though the current README summary did not enumerate a travel-specific scraper by name.
candidates.why_useful: General-purpose, well-maintained reference implementation for gap #17 (point-in-time SEC EDGAR tooling, alt-data evaluation methodology) that we could adapt directly rather than build from scratch.
candidates.license: unconfirmed (book companion, check for reuse terms)

candidates.name: pageview-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client for the Wikimedia Pageview REST API (e.g. pageviewapi.top('fr.wikipedia', 2015, 11, 14)); pulls daily/monthly per-article pageview counts for any Wikipedia article including "Airbnb", back to the API's 2015 start.
candidates.why_useful: Directly serves gap #5 (Wikipedia pageviews tooling as an engagement/interest proxy for Airbnb, distinct from the non-point-in-time Google Trends we already tried and found not to work).
candidates.size_hint: Thin client library, not a stored dataset

candidates.name: python-mwviews
candidates.what_it_holds: Tools for parsing and querying Wikimedia Foundation pageview data both from the online REST API and from the static bulk pageview dumps (allows longer/backfilled history than the API alone).
candidates.why_useful: Same gap #5 use case as pageview-api but adds access to Wikimedia's static dump files, which is useful for getting a longer point-in-time-stamped Airbnb pageview history in one pull rather than many API calls.

candidates.name: apprankings
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (42 stars, 10 forks) that pulls current App Store rankings from iTunes/App Store charts by country/category and writes results to CSV. No historical data committed — it is a live scraper you would run repeatedly to build your own history.
candidates.why_useful: Matches gap #5 (app download/ranking history as an engagement proxy for Airbnb's app); would need to be run going forward since it captures only present-day rankings, and Apple's own iTunes charts endpoint it hits is a public, non-Airbnb site so within scraping rules.

candidates.name: earnings_news_jar
candidates.what_it_holds: Code (59% Python, 41% Jupyter Notebook) accompanying the paper "How Is Earnings News Transmitted to Stock Prices?" — an academic replication package studying earnings-announcement information transmission, not company-specific but a methods reference for event-study construction around earnings prints.
candidates.why_useful: Relevant to gap #17 (event-study packages, earnings-implied-move estimators) as a citable academic methodology repo, though it is general-market rather than travel/OTA-specific.

candidates.name: post-no-preference/earnings (DoltHub)
candidates.what_it_holds: A Dolt (git-for-data) database on DoltHub described as holding "historical revenue and EPS estimates... data goes back to 2018 and is recorded weekly" — i.e. weekly-vintage analyst consensus snapshots, versioned like git commits so any past vintage is queryable/diffable. Not on GitHub itself but Dolt repos are git-clonable and DoltHub is a public, free host.
candidates.why_useful: If it covers ABNB/BKNG/EXPE, this is close to a direct hit on gap #4 (historical analyst-consensus snapshots with true point-in-time versioning via Dolt's commit history) — worth a follow-up check of ticker coverage since ABNB has only traded since Dec 2020.

candidates.name: airdna (API Evangelist profile)
candidates.what_it_holds: Not a data repo — an independent third-party API-surface profile/documentation of AirDNA's commercial API (which tracks 10M+ listings across 120,000+ markets: occupancy, revenue, ADR, RevPAR, booking lead time, length of stay, active listings, forward pricing 12-60 months). No data committed; just documents that the paid API exists and what fields it exposes.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the field list AirDNA sells (useful if the team ever budgets for a paid AirDNA sample) but is not itself a usable free dataset for gap #2 (realized ADR/occupancy).
candidates.geography: Global (120K+ markets per AirDNA's own marketing)

candidates.name: saturndatacloud/datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: A multi-industry sample-dataset repo (8 stars) advertising "alternative data in eCommerce, retailer, automotive, airlines, hotels, restaurants, real estate in 10+ countries." Confirmed automotive folders hold Tesla charging-station/store locations, Blink charging stations, used Tesla sales, and Carvana sales; Hotel/Restaurant/Airline folders exist in the directory tree but their specific file contents could not be confirmed from the landing page in this pass.
candidates.why_useful: Plausibly touches gaps #8 (hotel supply/demand) and #10 (airline capacity) if the hotel/airline folders hold real committed CSVs rather than placeholders — needs a direct directory listing (gh or WebFetch on the subfolder) to confirm before relying on it.

candidates.name: ABNB-Deep-Learning-Volatility
candidates.what_it_holds: A deep-learning volatility-forecasting project for ABNB stock that uses (with a Hugging Face fallback loader) the "nateraw/airbnb-stock-price-2" Hugging Face dataset for historical ABNB share-price data.
candidates.why_useful: Low incremental value — we already hold daily ABNB prices; only worth a line because it points at a specific, named Hugging Face dataset (nateraw/airbnb-stock-price-2) in case that dataset has a longer or differently-cleaned history than our current source.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Duplicates our existing daily ABNB price series

candidates.name: python-expedia-hotel-booking-searches
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis of the classic Kaggle "Expedia Hotel Recommendations" competition search-log dataset (user aggregate purchase history and hotel prices vs. nights-stay outcomes, fields like srch_saturday_night_bool). This is search-intent/click data from ~2013-2014, not company-level KPI data.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: it is old, user-level search-log data rather than an OTA volume/KPI series, but the underlying Kaggle dataset (Expedia, 37M+ rows) is a genuine large historical travel-search dataset that in principle could be mined for seasonality/demand patterns as a very rough competitor-OTA demand proxy.
candidates.size_hint: Kaggle source dataset is tens of millions of rows

candidates.name: stonkytonkydashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: A point-in-time consensus-earnings methodology repo for 10 semiconductor/tech names (Broadcom, Alphabet, NVIDIA, SK hynix, Samsung, Micron, Sandisk, ASML, Apple, BESI) — universe.csv, analyst_candidates.csv (35 company-analyst pairs), forecast_samples.csv (16 sample observations from 2021 and 2026 reports), source_manifest.csv with checksums, missing_data_dates.csv. 13,928 daily closes, 1,173 annual EPS observations across 350 dated "model snapshots" that separately tag broker forecasts, consensus, management guidance, and model scenarios by publication date. Full underlying broker PDFs (396) and extracted observations (2,420) are explicitly NOT committed — only a 16-row sample is public.
candidates.why_useful: Not travel/OTA data at all (semiconductors), but its schema for distinguishing broker-forecast vs. consensus vs. management-guidance vs. model-scenario observations, each stamped with a publication date, is a directly reusable template for our own L0 vintage register discipline (rule #2) — worth citing as a methods comparator even though we cannot use its data.
candidates.time_coverage: unconfirmed full range; sample rows from 2021 and 2026
candidates.size_hint: Only 16 rows of consensus data are actually public; rest excluded

notes: Hard blocker this run: the shared WebSearch tool budget (200/session, apparently shared across concurrent scout subagents) was already exhausted before I could issue a single WebSearch call, so I had to fall back to WebFetch against search-engine result pages. github.com/search was 429-rate-limited for the full session (Retry-After: 3600s), so no live GitHub code/repo search was possible either — I relied on github.com/topics/<tag> listing pages (not rate-limited) plus Brave/Bing/DuckDuckGo/Mojeek/Yahoo via WebFetch. Bing consistently returned generic airbnb.com marketing pages regardless of query (looked like a bot-detection fallback SERP, not real results) and DuckDuckGo HTML endpoints hit CAPTCHA every time — both were dead ends. Brave (search.brave.com) via WebFetch was the only search engine that returned genuine, query-relevant results, but it started 429-rate-limiting after ~10 queries in this session and never recovered within the remaining time. Given these constraints, coverage of this theme is meaningfully incomplete versus a normal `gh search` pass — a follow-up scout with a working `gh search code/repos` (once the org-wide rate limit resets) or a WebSearch budget should re-run this theme's keyword list, especially: 'nowcasting MIDAS DFM travel demand github', 'Zillow ZORI github mirror', 'Reddit airbnb pushshift dump github', 'NCLH advance ticket sales dataset', 'Chinese short-term-rental Tujia Xiaozhu data github', and a direct look at rsanjabi/short-term-rentals-warehouse's commit history / release assets to confirm whether raw pre-2023 Inside Airbnb files are actually retrievable (this is the single highest-value lead found and needs `gh` or git-clone verification, not just WebFetch summarization, since WebFetch could not see file-level repo contents beyond the README).
